banks.detail: October a hold at ~84-85% (CME FedWatch, Oct 21; Kalshi hold 89%) — blackout confirmed, no Fed speakers. December hike ~90%. 20-yr auction (Oct 21): $13B at 5.469% — record high since the tenor's May-2020 reintroduction; tailed WI 5.460% by 0.9bp (4th tail in a row, improved on Sept's 2bp); B/C 2.73 (vs 2.57 Sept); indirects 58.2% (avg 65.2% — soft foreign demand); directs record 31.6%. Dow Jones/WSJ: 'softer-than-expected'; Barron's: little market reaction. 10Y 5.12%, 2Y 4.79% (FRED DGS10/DGS2, Oct 20). The housing soft patch (starts 1.221M miss, pending home sales -7.3% record low, ADP 18.5K) vs the hot inflation week (import prices +8.1% y/y). Friday: 10Y 4.994% (baystreet, Oct 23) — steadied after Thursday's 19.5bp plunge; Dec-hike pricing eased to ~80% (FXStreet, Oct 23). Friday close: 10Y 5.00% (+4bp), 2Y 4.69% (marketbriefer) — yields reversed part of Thursday's 19.5bp haven plunge on hot PMIs + oil. Hyperscaler earnings share the tape with the FOMC: Alphabet + Microsoft Wed after the close, Amazon Thu. Oct 27 (FXEmpire): DXY near a one-week high ~102.04 as five central-bank decisions in three days plus the UK Budget keep traders cautious; CME Dec-hike odds ~73% (Monday) vs ~80%+ last week. Oct 28: HELD 3.75-4.00% (10-2; Cook + Hammack for a hike). Warsh presser: 2Y pulled back to 4.726% (-1bp), 10Y 5.007% (+1bp); DXY slipped to ~102.05 off its two-week high; stocks +0.2% (Reuters/Forex.com: Warsh fell short of a full hawkish December hint). December hike ~86% CME post-decision.
banks.summary: The Fed held in October (10-2, two hawkish dissents) and left December open; markets price a December hike at ~70%. Recent inflation has run hot, which keeps the dollar supported while markets wait.

December: further hike ~45% (swaps via Reuters); a second hike fully discounted by January. Loonie +0.1% to 1.4035 post-decision; Can 2Y hit a 2-year high 3.441%.

USD/CAD 1.4058, flat into the close. BMO/RBC/Desjardins all on hike calls. banks.summary: The Bank of Canada is priced ~75-80% to hike to 2.50% on October 28 after a hot September CPI, but TD and Rabobank both dissent and expect a hold. The decision lands Wednesday morning with the Monetary Policy Report.

banks.detail: October-28 hike ~98% to 3.00% (Reuters, Oct 22 — up from ~80-81% Oct 21; Finimize 89% Oct 21; ceo.com.pl 81%; BNZ/Westpac/ASB 80-85%). 50bp of hikes before end-February now priced at 100% (Reuters, Oct 22). Q3 CPI (Oct 21 4:45pm CT): 0.7% q/q vs 0.8% fcst (prev 1.5%); 3.7% y/y vs 3.8% fcst (from 4.1%) — below the RBNZ's 3.9% projection but still above the 1–3% target; Westpac: firm core inflation 'will give the RBNZ pause for thought.' NZD dipped to $0.5692 on the print. GDT Event 414 powder-led firm: WMP +4.4% ($3,760/t), SMP +3.4% — positive terms-of-trade read. Oct 28: surprise 4-3 HOLD at 2.75% — first time outside the pandemic the RBNZ held while markets priced >70% for a hike (Reuters Morning Bid); NZD fell to $0.5585 (-1.7% intraday, Finnhub low 0.5580). Statement: inflation above target largely on high global fuel costs; bank 'will adjust the OCR as needed'.
banks.summary: The RBNZ surprised markets by holding at 2.75% on October 28 in a 4-3 vote — but it was a hawkish hold: every member agreed further tightening is likely, and December 9 is live.

banks.name: European Central Bank
banks.priced: Oct 29: HELD at 2.50% (deposit; main refi 2.65%, marginal lending 2.90%) as expected (Reuters poll 70/73 for hold); statement data-dependent and meeting-by-meeting, no pre-commitment. Lagarde presser: the direction of travel is 'clear' and a hike was debated but unanimously deferred to December; Reuters sources: a Dec 17 hike is now 'all but certain', with a pause thereafter as higher yields bite (ECB estimates: the yield rise cuts 2027-28 growth ~100bp and inflation ~90bp). Same morning, Lagarde announced she steps down Feb 7, 2027, nine months early; succession starts immediately. December: hike ~86%+ (64/73 economists in the Reuters poll; market ~84-88% pre-decision). France: OAT-Bund ~167-177bp; S&P reviews France Nov 27.

banks.detail: October-29 hold virtually certain — Reuters Oct-8 poll: 70 of 73 economists expect a hold at 2.50%. December hike ~76% (ECB Watch, ~Oct-15 vintage; the earlier ~88% poll read is stale) — Commerzbank: 'market is pricing in one [hike] for December and slightly more than one additional hike by mid-2027'. Lagarde: no major-wire carry of new rate remarks indexed today. German PPI +6.7% y/y beat (vs 6.2%); EZ final CPI 3.8% confirmed. Eurozone natural gas >EUR 90/MWh (first since Dec 2022) — fresh energy-cost pressure. France: revenue-section vote postponed (first reading to Oct 27; FinMin Lescure floated Article 49.3); OAT 4.948% (+2.9bp, WSJ/Tradeweb); OAT-Bund ~153bp; Moody's reviews France Friday (Aa3 negative — markets expect a one-notch cut to A1). EUR/USD 1.1233, flat. IMF (Oct 16 regular Europe report): at least one further 25bp ECB hike in 2026 is warranted to keep core inflation contained; 'further tightening likely warranted' beyond 2026. https://www.reuters.com/business/imf-expects-least-one-more-25-bps-ecb-rate-hike-2026-2026-10-16/ Friday: France 10Y 5.14% (highest since July 2002); OAT-Bund 170-177bp (highest since 2011); Moody's reviews France (Aa3 neg) after the US close (~3pm CT) — downgrade priced in, outlook the variable (Reuters). Panetta: yield climb a growth headwind, not a crisis (baystreet). Flash PMIs all missed — France comp 48.4 back in contraction. Moody's decision (Oct 23 evening): Aa3 affirmed with negative outlook — the downgrade to A1 that most economists expected did not come; the agency wants a deficit-cutting 2027 budget and sees French debt topping 120% of GDP in 2027; S&P next reviews France Nov 27. Newsquawk: the Oct-29 statement may be 'even more non-committal than typical'; growing chatter about Lagarde's departure as a presser talking point. Oct 29 outcome: held at 2.50% as expected; Lagarde signaled the December direction clearly and announced her Feb 7, 2027 departure; Reuters sources call a Dec 17 hike all but certain.
banks.summary: The ECB is expected to hold in October and is leaning toward a hike in December, because inflation is at a three-year high. France's budget trouble is the main thing weighing on the euro.

banks.detail: October 29-30 a hold — OIS ~88-90% hold odds; Reuters Oct 20 (four BoJ sources): the bank may upgrade its inflation forecast and hold steady. December hike ~80% (Japan Times/Bloomberg, Oct 21, via ex-BoJ executive Maeda, who expects Dec then Mar/Apr) — a step up from the ~73-74% read. Ueda's 'quite close' to 2% leans December, not October. Sep trade deficit -¥536.6bn vs -¥181bn fc (exports +16.7% missed +20.1%). USD/JPY 158.10-158.18, flat — the BOJ hawkish-forecast headline capping the topside. Sep national core CPI 2.1% y/y inline (Aug 1.7%) — first above the BoJ's 2% target in nine months; core-core 2.4% (vs 2.3% fcst) cements December-hike pricing. USD/JPY bounced to ~156.88 off the 156.08 one-month low; intervention chatter in Friday wires (Reuters). Oct 27: Japan services PPI held at 3.7% y/y inline (Reuters, London morning); Finance Minister Katayama warned Tuesday the government stands ready to take decisive action in the currency market. Oct 30 outcome: held at 1.25% (8-1, Takata for 1.50%); Outlook Report called the 2% target reached, FY2027 core CPI raised to 2.6%; December hike ~80%.
banks.summary: The BoJ keeps signalling that more rate hikes are coming, probably in December rather than October. Higher Japanese rates would narrow the gap with the US and support the yen.

banks.summary: The RBA is now heavily priced to hike to 4.85% on November 3 after a Q3 CPI that ran hotter than its own forecasts. Bullock says the board will debate whether four hikes this year are enough.

banks.summary: The Bank of England is almost certain to raise rates on November 5, and the debate is already about December. Healey's first Budget on Wednesday lands eight days before the decision.

banks.detail: Holding at 0.00%; December cut risk on the table (PPI +0.3% vs 0.6% miss — disinflation intact). September discussions summary (released Oct 22, 02:30 CT): widening rate differentials + low volatility mean a cheaper hedge against franc strength — the franc's carry-trade appeal acknowledged; the board's readiness to intervene has eased (tolerates franc weakness). USD/CHF ~0.824 (-0.1%). Haven bid fired on Gulf escalation but the franc was not the leader — the yen was.
banks.summary: The SNB's September write-up (out Oct 22) says the franc now looks like a carry-trade target and the board is less ready to fight a weak franc — it tolerates franc softness. Rates stay at zero; December could still see a cut. The franc keeps moving more on global fear than Swiss news.
